A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, mathematical statements, Table 1, algorithms, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison despite substantial formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical results, proofs, algorithms, and analytical comparisons of regret bounds. Neither the main text nor the appendices contain original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains a theoretical paper. Inspection of the main text and Appendices A–E establishes that no experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

M1.justification: The exponential mapping, surrogate potential, BQND estimator, and Algorithm 2 are unchanged. The SO-OGA, Improved Ader, and feedback-reduction procedures in the appendices are also retained; the new explanations do not alter their steps.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical evaluation tasks. The same optimization domain and feedback settings are analyzed theoretically; newly mentioned applications and future extensions are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparators. Table 1 retains the same analytical comparisons with Thang and Srivastav (2021), Zhang et al. (2023), and Pedramfar et al. (2024), relabeled 2024a in v2.

E3.justification: Neither PDF contains experimental protocols, data splits, training budgets, or evaluation procedures. The retained oracle settings, regret definitions, and theoretical algorithm parameter choices do not introduce an evaluation change.

E4.justification: Neither version includes ablations, sensitivity experiments, robustness evaluations, error analyses, or case studies. The appendix proofs and reductions are retained; v2's added mechanism discussion is explanatory.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Expectations and estimator bounds remain theoretical properties, rather than empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 and Propositions 1–7 retain their numerical regret orders and comparisons. The existing bandit discrepancies also persist: Table 1 gives T^(4/5), whereas Proposition 6 gives T^(2/3) and Proposition 7 gives a dynamic T^(5/6) dependence. No empirical results are added.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, definitions, theorem statements, and proofs in the main text and Appendices A–E are substantively unchanged. v2 removes v1's explicit expectation expression for F, which merely restates its retained integral definition. Renaming upper linearizability and adding intuitive Remark 2 do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: v2's abstract explicitly adds the novelty claim of the first non-Frank-Wolfe algorithms exceeding a 1/4 approximation for this setting. The contribution summary also highlights BQND separately. The central 1/e-linearizability, single-query efficiency, and static, adaptive, and dynamic regret claims remain.

C2.justification: New Remark 2 explains feasibility of the exponential mapping and cancellation through the surrogate potential. Section 6 adds specific limitations concerning adversarial information, unresolved limited-feedback lower bounds, and extension to weakly DR-submodular functions. The online/offline approximation gap was already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: The algorithm pseudocode, sampling distribution, step-size prescriptions, smoothing parameters, and appendix implementation descriptions are retained. Neither version supplies experimental hardware details or code/data access information, and v2 adds no such resources.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially reframes the work around the general-convex 1/4 threshold and dependence on Frank-Wolfe methods. Added literature covers general-convex optimality, phase retrieval, one-sided smooth optimization, and weak DR-submodularity. Section 4 also explicitly identifies Lemma 1 as a constant-path specialization of Buchbinder and Feldman's result, clarifying its relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The technical-novelty discussion, contribution list, related work, and conclusion are substantially rewritten or expanded. v2 adds a limitations discussion and Impact Statement and changes linearizability terminology. The main section sequence and Appendices A–E remain intact.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes a conference-style document with a two-column main text, running headers, revised typography, and a redesigned author block. Table 1 and algorithm displays are restyled and repositioned, while appendices remain single-column. These are extensive layout changes without new figures or result tables.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through clearer attribution of Lemma 1, explanation of the structural reduction, and specific limitations in Section 6. These are useful but limited gains: the mathematical development is unchanged, and the bandit-bound inconsistencies between Table 1 and Propositions 6–7 remain unresolved.
